solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Creation of painter?

parts.note: surface reading: an artist producing a picture
setter's reading: a painter is also the line that ties a small boat to a quay, so its creation is the craft of twisting cord

explanation.walkthrough: A painter in sailing is the rope at a dinghy's bow; the question mark flags that the artist is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade of twisting fibres into cordage is what produces a boat's painter, so its creation is that craft.

clue.text: Essentially said Stalin demolished Axis nationals

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked apart, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order
essentially means at the core, so only the central letters of the next word are used

parts.note: the two middle letters of said
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wartime account of the Soviet leader crushing soldiers of the Axis powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy was one of the Axis powers in the Second World War, alongside Germany and Japan, so its people are Axis nationals.

clue.text: Ring found in small arachnid embryo segment

indicators.note: something found in another is placed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a ring is the round letter O
a mite is a tiny eight-legged arachnid

explanation.surface: A biologist spots a ring-shaped structure in a tiny spider-like creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring goes after the S and before the creature, sitting inside the combined small arachnid.
explanation.definitionFit: In zoology a somite is one of the paired blocks of tissue that divide an embryo along its length.

clue.text: Aviator's rather a maniac

indicators.note: a maniac behaves wildly, so the letters before it are thrown into a crazy new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that some pilot is rather a madman.
explanation.walkthrough: Amelia Earhart was the American pilot famous for flying the Atlantic solo and vanishing over the Pacific in 1937; 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia Earhart is a famous example of a pilot, the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Tragic husband wearing ripped panties

indicators.note: one who is wearing clothes is inside them, so the first piece goes within the second
ripped means torn apart, so the letters of the garment are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A sad scene of a husband dressed in torn women's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tragic' looks like a comment on the husband, but it is the definition: thespian as an adjective means to do with drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespis is credited as the founder of Greek tragedy, so thespian as an adjective means dramatic, relating to tragedy.

clue.text: Shakespearean king's medal prone to be stripped?

indicators.note: stripping removes the outer covering, so the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
prone without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A wry question whether a Shakespearean monarch's decoration is about to be taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British order of chivalry awarded as a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so a royal character from Shakespeare.

clue.text: Nothing omitted in utter depravity

indicators.note: omitted means left out, so a letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: to utter is to voice, a verb
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A moralist's phrase: nothing left out in a picture of total wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' reads as the adjective meaning complete, but it is the verb to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice is immoral or wicked behaviour, a direct synonym for depravity.

clue.text: One making adjustments to frame set a photo askew

indicators.note: askew means crooked or out of line, so the letters are set in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone straightening a picture frame after a photo has been hung crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The frame is the body's skeleton, not a picture frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath manipulates bones and joints, adjusting the body's skeletal frame by hand.

clue.text: Spirit of writer with upset stomach

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and stomach points to the middle, so the central part of the word is turned round

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a common crossword writer

explanation.surface: An author's mood soured by indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: Biro is the British everyday name for a ballpoint pen; only its two middle letters swap round.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or vivacity, the same lively energy as spirit.

clue.text: Attend to passing around large wind instruments at first

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word is wrapped about the rest

parts.note: passing is a polite word for dying
L is the abbreviation for large

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letters of the words just before it

parts.note: first letters of wind and instruments

explanation.surface: Instructions to deal with the brass section by walking round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with a matter is to attend to it, take care of it; both are phrasal verbs.

clue.text: Ice sphere encircled by band

indicators.note: something encircled by another is surrounded by it, so it sits inside

parts.note: a set is a band or group of people
an orb is a sphere

explanation.surface: A frozen ball wrapped in a strip of material.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a water ice, a frozen fruit dessert; 'ice' is a standard name for such desserts.

clue.text: Boy at heart has a passion for rowing

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of boy
taken as written
a rage is a passion, as in a rage for something

explanation.surface: A lad who is mad keen on rowing.
explanation.walkthrough: A rare word: the second 'for' is just the link; the surface 'passion for rowing' joins pieces across the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarage is an old poetic word for the action or motion of oars, that is, rowing.

clue.text: Again inflame ire and get in fight

indicators.note: a fight is a scrap or brawl, so the letters before it are knocked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
joins the two pieces of fodder

explanation.surface: Stirring anger again by joining a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To reignite is to set alight a second time, and figuratively to stir up feelings anew.

clue.text: Intimidated by endless doctrine in series of online posts

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a thread is a chain of replies in an online forum

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a tenet is a doctrine or principle

explanation.surface: Someone bullied by dogma pushed in a long chain of internet posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Threatened can mean menaced or frightened by threats, the same sense as intimidated.

clue.text: Root traps little gun dog at last

parts.note: a gin is a snare, so traps are gins

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of each of the words just before it

parts.note: final letters of little, gun and dog

explanation.surface: A small gundog digs and catches its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun dog' reads as a retriever, but the three words each give only their last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginseng is a plant valued for its medicinal root, which is the part sold and eaten.

clue.text: Closely related team left in British estate?

parts.note: near relatives are closely related
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A family group left behind on a British country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate here is an estate car, a station wagon; Britons drive on the left, so the nearside of a car is its left.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the nearside of a vehicle is the side nearest the kerb, which is the left-hand side.

clue.text: Defends oneself against all points penned by curt idiot

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed by it, as in a pen
curt suggests cut short, so the word that follows loses its last letter

parts.note: arse is British slang for a fool
the four compass points, north, south, west, east

explanation.surface: Someone fending off criticism from a rude fool on every point.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points go in after the A of the shortened slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer charges is to respond to and rebut them, so answers means defends oneself against.

clue.text: Thoroughly examined cyst colour before start of operation

parts.note: a wen is a cyst on the skin
a tint is a colour or shade

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: first letter of operation

explanation.surface: A surgeon checks the colour of a cyst before operating.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into a subject is to investigate it in detail, so went into means examined thoroughly.

clue.text: Adopt juvenile, finally, with partner

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of juvenile
a spouse is a married partner

explanation.surface: A couple deciding to adopt a child together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adopt' reads as taking in a child, but it means taking up a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause or belief is to adopt and support it.

clue.text: Wherein soldiers may plunge intellectuals

definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptic: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into the open tops of boiled eggs
second meaning: clever, bookish people, in slang

explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are thin fingers of buttered toast, a British breakfast dipped into a soft-boiled egg; the military picture is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term for highbrow, studious people likens their domed heads to eggs.

clue.text: Bends part of leg and eg back when cycling

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so the short word is read from right to left
cycling means going round, so the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: the shin is the front of the lower leg
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cyclist's knee and leg bending as they pedal.
explanation.walkthrough: Join the leg part and the turned abbreviation, then move the front S to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinges are the jointed fittings on which a door bends or swings, so they are bends in a broad sense.

clue.text: Bosnia developed art form

indicators.note: something developed has changed its form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Balkan country building up its artistic culture.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees in pots.

clue.text: Boast about case of old, old raid

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the boast wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to brag is to boast

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: outer letters of the first old

explanation.surface: Someone bragging about an ancient raid.
explanation.walkthrough: A rare word: bodrag is an obsolete term for a hostile incursion, especially an Irish border raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodrag is an archaic word, found in Spenser, for a raid or hostile incursion.

clue.text: Corrects setter, going over targeted goals

indicators.note: going over suggests flipping over, so the setter's word is turned round

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
ends are aims or goals one targets

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter fixing mistakes after reviewing the aims.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors, so emends means corrects.

clue.text: Fashion magazine cleared out a thousand lines

indicators.note: to line something is to sit along its inside, so one piece goes inside the other
cleared out means emptied, so all inner letters go and only the outer two remain

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
K, for kilo, is a thousand

explanation.surface: A style magazine emptying its stock of a thousand printed lines.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to make it, shape or form it; both are verbs.

clue.text: Cleric roared in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest bellowing his sermon over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordainer is a bishop or other churchman who ordains new priests, so a cleric.

clue.text: This contributes to whisky export

indicators.note: something that contributes to a phrase forms a part of it, so the letters sit within the next words

parts.note: runs across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A pointer to a place that adds to whisky sold abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: the Hebridean island is home to the Talisker distillery, so it contributes to Scotch exports.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye, an island in Scotland's Inner Hebrides, makes single malt whisky that is sold worldwide.

clue.text: Demolish books in very bad English

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the next one

parts.note: dismal means very poor or dreadful
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Criticising books written in dreadful English.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle a structure is to take it apart, so it means demolish.
